item.title: Diagram of Geodesic Intervals in $C'(1/8)$-Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.00095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a group characterized by a small cancellation $C'(1/8)$-presentation. We study the structure of its Cayley graph, specifically geodesic intervals and digons. We prove that all geodesic segments $[x,y]$ of length $n$ can be covered by finitely many simple geodesic digons with pairwise $C'(1/8)$-short lower intersections whose lower sides lie on a common geodesic segment $[x,y]$. This is a generalization of a proposition of Kharlampovich-Sklinos (arXiv:2106.05461) for random groups. We then bound this resulting diagram of digons, showing that the total perimeter of its cells and its edge count is bounded by $n$, and the cycle rank is equal to the number of distinct cell contours. Thus, although there may be many different geodesics, the size of their union is bounded linearly in the distance between their endpoints. The constant is independent of the number and lengths of the defining relators. In particular, the estimate applies to infinite presentations with unbounded relator lengths. From this we get a consequence for growth, allowing us to compare the number of geodesic words with the number of group elements of the same length.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Hoffmann

item.title: A Computational Verification of the Markov Uniqueness Conjecture for $z\leq 10^{500000}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.01007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe a finite computational verification of Markov Uniqueness Conjecture for normalized positive integer solutions of $x^2+y^2+z^2=3xyz$ with $z \leq 10^{500000}$. The archived run reports $239\,536\,376\,556$ triples with distinct maximal coordinates.The method combines a disjoint tree decomposition, certified fixed-point range bounds, a deterministic 48-bit candidate screen,and replay modulo $2^{128}$. We give the mathematical justification and a reproducibility procedure covering package checks,retained-data auditing, and a full rerun. The conclusion depends on correct execution of the exhaustive screen and replay; the retained audit does not regenerate the deleted screening buckets.
item.dc:creator: Hu Tan, Ying Zhang

item.title: Linear-exponent bounds for the automatic complexity of rational diagonals modulo prime powers
item.description: arXiv:2611.01481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and let $G$ be the diagonal of $N/Q$ in $m$ variables over the $p$-adic integers, with $Q(0)$ a unit. We prove that the $p$-kernel of the coefficients of $G$ modulo $p^\alpha$ has size $K_\alpha(G)\le p^{(|J|+1)\alpha-1}+(p^\alpha-1)/(p-1)$, where $J$ is an explicit finite support set determined by the Newton polytopes of $N$ and $Q$, and $|J|\le\prod_i(h_i+1)$ for $h_i=\max(\deg_{z_i}N,\deg_{z_i}Q)$. Thus the minimal automaton has $p^{O(\alpha)}$ states for fixed input and prime. The general upper bounds of Rowland and Yassawi have exponents that are cubic in $\alpha$ for Furstenberg series and of order $\alpha^{m+1}$ for diagonals in $m$ variables. The proof combines a $\delta$-decomposition with synchronous Cartier sections and a count of compatible histories; it requires no smoothness or ordinarity assumption. We give explicit transitions and derive bounds for Furstenberg series. For the Furstenberg series $F$ of $bx^2y^2+(1+ax+dx^2)y+cx^2$ with odd $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove $K_\alpha(F)\ge9\cdot8^\alpha/(64\alpha-32)$ and $\lim_{\alpha\to\infty}\alpha^{-1}\log_2K_\alpha(F)=3$. This exponent result rests on primitive reachability, parameter-independent normalized window frames, and an overlap estimate certified in a finite quotient of a rational Cartier lattice. An appendix also proves that the zero orbit in the Rowland-Yassawi automaton for $x^2y^2+(1+x+x^2)y+x^2$ has exactly $2^{\alpha+1}+\alpha+1$ states, resolving their orbit-size conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Alex Shvets

item.title: Certain Representation of the Rationals With Bounded Partial Quotients
item.description: arXiv:2504.07970v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define a new representation for a subset of rational numbers and prove that each real number \( x \notin (-1,1) \) can be approximated arbitrarily well by rational numbers which have only \( 2 \)'s and \( 1 \)'s in their representation.
item.dc:creator: Franciszek Kobus

item.title: On noncontinuous bisymmetric strictly monotone operations
item.description: arXiv:2601.16247v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct bisymmetric, partially strictly increasing binary operations on real intervals which are not continuous. This shows that continuity cannot be removed from the classical characterization of bisymmetric quasi-sums due to Acz\'el and Dhombres. Our examples are operations of the form \[ F(x,y)=f^{-1}(\alpha f(x)+\beta f(y)), \] where $\alpha,\beta>0$ and $\alpha+\beta\neq1$. The generating map $f$ is chosen as a strictly increasing bijection from an interval onto a two-component subset of $\mathbb{R}$ separated by a gap. The range is directly invariant under the relevant weighted sums, while the gap produces a jump of $f$ and hence discontinuity of every one-variable section. As a consequence, we obtain discontinuous associative and strictly increasing operations on intervals, and we extend the construction to the multivariate case. In the opposite direction, we prove that if a symmetric bisymmetric strictly increasing operation is reflexive at two points of an interval, then it is automatically continuous on the segment between them and coincides there with a quasi-arithmetic mean.
item.dc:creator: Gergely Kiss

item.title: Khayyam's Choices of Conics
item.description: arXiv:2605.13876v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the late eleventh century, Omar Khayyam gave a systematic classification of, and solutions to, cubic equations by means of intersecting conic sections. His work is often retold in modern Cartesian language, where each cubic is reduced to equations of certain curves whose intersection determines solutions in the Cartesian plane. In this paper, we retain the first part of the standard modern treatment of Khayyam: translating his verbal algebra into modern symbolic algebra. But instead of interpreting the resulting equations as curves in a Cartesian plane, we interpret them as Khayyam himself did, as relations between positive geometrical magnitudes represented by conics in the Apollonian sense. On this basis, and using a purpose-designed colour scheme, we reconstruct, in a compact treatment, his solutions to all the cubic equations treated by Khayyam. The reconstruction brings to light a hidden feature of the treatise and draws a sharp line between the geometrization of algebra as practised by Khayyam, on the one hand, and the geometrization of algebra developed by Fermat and Descartes, on the other.
item.dc:creator: Amir Asghari

item.title: Admissible qx+1 Sequences, Semiconvergents, and Rational Catalan Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2609.22303v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $q\geq3$ be odd and put $m_r=\lfloor r\log_2q\rfloor$. We count parity sequences with exactly $r$ entries equal to $1$ for which the coefficient in the $qx+1$ iteration first drops below $1$ at step $m_r+1$. Their number $a_q(r)$ also counts the corresponding residue classes modulo $2^{m_r+1}$. By classifying increasing integer sequences according to the first index at which they exceed a prescribed bound, we obtain a recurrence which, for $q=3$, establishes the five- or six-term block pattern conjectured in 2015, allowing a shorter final block. We establish the sharp inequalities \[ \frac1r\binom{m_r-1}{r-1}\leq a_q(r)\leq\frac1r\binom{m_r}{r-1} \] Equality in the lower (respectively upper) bound occurs exactly when $\{r\log_2q\}$ is smaller (respectively larger) than all preceding fractional parts $\{j\log_2q\}$, $1\leq j<r$. These indices are characterized by denominators of convergents and semiconvergents from below and above; at these indices $r\geq2$, the values $a_q(r)$ are rational Catalan numbers. We also characterize the dependence on $q$ and prove, for each fixed odd $q\geq3$, that $a_q(r)=\Theta_q(r^{-3/2}B_q^r)$, where $B_q=(\log_2q)^{\log_2q}/(\log_2q-1)^{\log_2q-1}$. For $q=3$, this proves Hikawa's conjectured polynomial factor for the number of finite binary words of given weight for which the length of every nonempty prefix is smaller than $\log_2 3$ times the number of its ones.
item.dc:creator: Mike Winkler
